rewrites.title: Targeted epigenome editing and sufficiency tests at AP-1 sites
rewrites.description: Use CRISPR deletion of AP-1 motifs or dCas9-based editing at memory enhancers, plus ectopic AP-1 induction, to test whether AP-1 binding is necessary and sufficient to establish lasting accessibility, histone marks (H3K27ac), and enhanced re-induction, including pioneer-factor and BAF-complex dependence.

rewrites.title: Acute AP-1 degradation to separate initiation from maintenance
rewrites.description: Use degron-tagged (dTAG/AID) JUN/FOS or a dominant-negative (A-FOS) system to remove AP-1 at different times after the priming stimulus. If accessibility and the enhanced secondary transcriptional response persist after AP-1 loss, AP-1 is an initiator. If they collapse, it is a continuous maintainer.

rewrites.title: Single-cell multiome tracking of AP-1 activity and lineage inheritance
rewrites.description: Combine single-cell RNA/ATAC with lineage barcoding or live-cell AP-1 reporters to determine whether AP-1 activity states are inherited through cell divisions and heterogeneous across clones. Persistence across divisions without ongoing signal would support memory.

rewrites.title: Single-cell multiome tracking with lineage barcodes
rewrites.description: Run paired scRNA/scATAC-seq with live reporters of AP-1 activity and heritable barcodes across divisions after a transient stimulus. Test whether the primed state is inherited by daughter cells and whether it correlates with the AP-1 motif accessibility of a clone, separating a stable epigenetic state from ongoing signaling noise.

rewrites.title: Live-cell AP-1 dynamics and reporter readout
rewrites.description: Image endogenously tagged FOS/JUN, or an AP-1 transcriptional reporter, in single cells across repeated stimuli. Test whether the memory shows up as a persistent protein level, a change in dynamics, or a faster reporter induction, and whether it depends on cooperating factors or histone marks (H3K27ac, H3K4me1) checked by ChIP or CUT&Tag.

rewrites.title: Targeted epigenome editing of AP-1 sites to test sufficiency and necessity
rewrites.description: Use dCas9-based tools (KRAB or p300) or motif mutations through CRISPR base editing to alter specific AP-1-bound enhancers that stay accessible after the signal. Test whether closing them erases the primed response, and whether forced AP-1 binding or opening creates a memory without the stimulus. Readouts are the gene expression response to re-challenge and the persistence of chromatin marks, which would show causality at single loci.

rewrites.title: Transient stimulus with delayed re-challenge
rewrites.description: Expose cells to a brief stimulus (e.g., TNF, EGF, or PMA), let it wash out for hours to days, then re-stimulate and measure the transcriptional response (RNA-seq, nascent RNA) relative to naive cells. Compare the memory-linked response in wild-type cells and cells with AP-1 (FOS/JUN) knocked out or acutely degraded to see whether AP-1 is needed for the primed or altered response.

rewrites.title: Live-cell reporters and mathematical modeling of feedback
rewrites.description: Image endogenously tagged FOS/JUN and a downstream reporter in single cells during pulses of different duration and frequency. Fit bistable or positive-feedback models and test predictions, such as hysteresis and a threshold dose, by perturbing feedback loops (e.g., JUN autoregulation) to see if AP-1 dynamics alone can store state.

rewrites.title: Primed vs. naive re-stimulation challenge with acute AP-1 degradation
rewrites.description: Prime cells with a first stimulus, rest them, then restimulate and compare transcriptional output (RNA-seq, nascent PRO-seq) to naive cells; repeat with a degron (dTAG/AID) or dominant-negative (A-FOS) of FOS/JUN applied only during priming versus only during recall. If AP-1 is needed at priming to produce faster/stronger recall but not at recall, it acts as a memory-writing factor.

rewrites.title: Motif-specific synthetic perturbation of enhancers
rewrites.description: Use CRISPR to mutate or delete AP-1 motifs at specific memory-associated enhancers, or use dCas9 to recruit or block AP-1 there. Test the effect on retained accessibility and on the faster secondary response at the linked genes. Combine with reporter assays to show that the AP-1 site is necessary, and that adding it to a naive enhancer is sufficient, to produce memory.

rewrites.title: Single-cell multiome tracking of lineage-linked memory
rewrites.description: Perform paired scRNA/scATAC-seq, with lineage barcodes or live reporters, on cells at several times after a transient stimulus. Test whether AP-1 motif accessibility and target expression are inherited across cell divisions in clonal families, and whether they are bimodal, as expected for epigenetic memory.

rewrites.title: Time-resolved measurement of AP-1 dynamics and nucleosome turnover, with prolongation of AP-1 activity
rewrites.description: Perform time-resolved CUT&Tag for AP-1 factors, H3K27ac, and a nucleosome-turnover/histone-age label (e.g., SNAP-tag pulse-chase) across days after a transient stimulus, then fit models in which the delay between AP-1 loss and enhancer decay is the memory timescale. Then test causality by optogenetically or chemically prolonging AP-1 activity for a short window and checking whether the persistence time scales with it, which would show that the delay encodes the history.

rewrites.title: Transient stimulus then washout: persistence of AP-1 chromatin accessibility
rewrites.description: Expose cells (e.g., fibroblasts or keratinocytes) to a defined pulse of TPA, TNF or wounding signal, remove it, and track ATAC-seq, CUT&RUN for FOS/JUN, and H3K27ac at AP-1 motif sites over days to weeks. Memory is supported if accessibility and a faster, stronger transcriptional response to restimulation persist after signaling and AP-1 levels return to baseline. A second exposure is expected to differ from the first.

rewrites.title: Single-cell ATAC/CUT&Tag of AP-1 motif accessibility after transient stimulus
rewrites.description: Stimulate cells (e.g., epithelial or immune cells with a wound/inflammatory cue), remove the stimulus, and track at single-cell resolution which AP-1 (FOS/JUN) motif-bearing enhancers stay open for days to weeks. Persistent accessibility at specific sites, heterogeneous between cells, would indicate stored state; compare to unstimulated cells and to cells re-challenged later.

rewrites.title: Single-cell tracking of AP-1 activity and heritability
rewrites.description: Use live-cell AP-1 reporters or FOS/JUN imaging, combined with lineage tracing or single-cell multiome (RNA + ATAC) of sister cells. Test whether the primed state is bistable, is inherited across divisions, and decays with a measurable half-life. Heritability and a stable, all-or-none state would distinguish memory from a simple lingering response.

rewrites.title: AP-1 dimer composition and partner factors as a code for stimulus history
rewrites.description: AP-1 dimers (FOS/JUN/ATF/MAF families) combine with partner TFs (e.g., ETS, NFAT, lineage TFs) to produce composite motifs. Use paired perturbation of dimer composition and partner presence (CRISPRi/degron matrix) with ChIP/CUT&Tag and MPRA to test whether history is encoded in which dimer and partner pairs were engaged, a pattern neither input contains alone. Predict that a history-specific dimer/partner signature at enhancers can decode a cell's past stimulus from chromatin state with a classifier trained on known histories.

rewrites.title: Multiome profiling with pioneer-factor and cofactor perturbation
rewrites.description: Run single-cell RNA plus ATAC (multiome) on primed and naive cells, and link persistent accessible regions to the response on re-challenge. Perturb the AP-1 partners and chromatin remodelers that could provide the persistence, such as BAF/SWI-SNF, and test which are required for memory. Include Hi-C or Micro-C to see whether looping is kept.

rewrites.title: Primed vs. naive re-stimulation transcriptional response
rewrites.description: Compare RNA-seq and nascent transcription (PRO-seq/TT-seq) after a first versus second stimulus, with varying rest intervals between them, in wild-type and AP-1-perturbed cells. Faster or stronger induction of the same genes on re-challenge, with a decay constant that depends on AP-1 dosage, would quantify memory strength and duration.

rewrites.title: Chromatin accessibility memory after transient stimulus
rewrites.description: Stimulate cells (e.g., with TPA, growth factor, or injury signal), then wash out and perform ATAC-seq and AP-1 (FOS/JUN) CUT&RUN at time points over days to weeks. Persistent AP-1 motif-containing accessible sites after AP-1 levels return to baseline would indicate a retained memory state. Because the persistent sites are a sparse signal, they must be separated from noise by comparing against unstimulated controls and shuffled-motif backgrounds.

rewrites.title: Single-cell multiome lineage-tracked memory persistence
rewrites.description: Run paired scATAC and scRNA-seq with live reporters of AP-1 activity, using barcoded lineage tracing across cell divisions. This tests whether accessibility states are inherited clonally, whether memory is heterogeneous or bimodal, and whether it correlates with past AP-1 activity levels.
